# Building

Run `pocketone desktop build` in your app's folder, the one with `pb_hooks`, `pb_migrations` or `pb_public`. It embeds
those folders in a desktop app for each platform you ask for.

```sh
pocketone desktop build                                        # this machine's platform
pocketone desktop build --all                                  # all six below
pocketone desktop build --target windows/amd64,linux/amd64     # some of them
pocketone desktop build --out builds                           # somewhere other than dist/
pocketone desktop build --no-sign                              # skip the sign section
```

| Platform | `--target` | You get |
|---|---|---|
| macOS, Apple Silicon | `darwin/arm64` | `dist/darwin-arm64/<name>.app` and `<name>.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `darwin/amd64` | `dist/darwin-amd64/<name>.app` and `<name>.dmg` |
| Windows, x64 | `windows/amd64` | `dist/windows-amd64/<name>.exe` |
| Windows, Arm | `windows/arm64` | `dist/windows-arm64/<name>.exe` |
| Linux, x64 | `linux/amd64` | `dist/linux-amd64/<name>` |
| Linux, Arm | `linux/arm64` | `dist/linux-arm64/<name>` |

Each is one file (or one `.app` bundle) of about 40 MB, with your app and PocketOne inside. Windows builds open no
console window.

On a Mac, each macOS build also comes as a `.dmg`: the app and a link to Applications to drag it onto. With a `sign`
section in `pocketone.yaml`, every build is signed for you; see [Signing and sharing](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/desktop/signing).

## Name and size

`pocketone.yaml`'s `desktop` section names the app and sizes its window:

```yaml
desktop:
  name: Notes              # window title and file name; default: the folder's name
  id: dev.example.notes    # where each user's data lives; default: app.pocketone.<name>
  width: 900               # starting window size; default 1024 × 768
  height: 640
```

Choose the `id` once and keep it. It names the folder each user's data lives in, so a new `id` is a new, empty app for
everyone who installed the old one.

## The build image

Builds run in Docker, in the build image for your `pocketone`'s version: `ghcr.io/pocketonehq/pocketone-build:v<version>`,
pulled the first time. It holds Go, PocketOne's source and every dependency, vendored, so once it's here builds work
offline, and the same `pocketone` version always builds the same app.

`pocketone desktop build` mounts your app folder and the output folder into it, builds every platform there, and
keeps Go's build cache in a Docker volume (`pocketone-build-cache`), so rebuilds take seconds. On a Mac it then signs
the macOS bundles ad hoc, so they run on that Mac.

A development `pocketone`, built from a PocketOne checkout, has no published image. It builds its own,
`pocketone-build:dev`, from that checkout the first time (a minute or two). `pocketone desktop image` rebuilds it after
you change the source.

## Without Docker

With Go 1.27 or newer and a PocketOne checkout, `--local` builds with your own Go instead:

```sh
pocketone desktop build --local --all                        # inside the checkout
pocketone desktop build --local --source ~/src/pocketone     # anywhere else (or set P1_SOURCE)
```

It needs no C compiler either: every platform cross-compiles with plain Go.
